messages:
ashley: Quick question — I'm rolling a terraform change to switch the inference svc to NLB passthrough (GatewayAPI TCPRoute) and the healthchecks are failing during canary.

ashley: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/3212

ashley: Service uses headless + port mapping. Short snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: inference
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
    - name: health
      port: 15020
      targetPort: 15020
``` 

ashley: Gateway tcpRoute backend is pointing to servicePort 15020. NLB target group is target_type = ip.

sre-bot: healthcheck: target 10.0.12.7:15020 connection_reset (x7)

devon: Two quick things to confirm:
- Is the k8s Service actually exposing the pod IP on 15020 (not just nodePort)?
- Which target_type is the TG? you said ip — then the NLB will hit pod IP:port directly, so kube-proxy mode / headless + ports must match.

raj: Also check service port naming: with GatewayAPI/TCPRoute we expect numeric port refs or correct port names. If you name the port `http` it can confuse L7 assumptions elsewhere. For pure TCP passthrough use a tcp-y or raw name and reference by number from the route.

ashley: Hmm, we used `http` for 8080 and `health` for 15020. The pod has envoy sidecar listening on 15020 for healthchecks, but kube-proxy in our environment is iptables mode — headless + NodePort combination made me worry about where the NLB checks land.

devon: If TG target_type = ip, NLB calls pod IP:15020 directly. That requires the pod to be Ready and 15020 exposed on the pod network. If kube-proxy or ipvs is rewriting, health checks can get reset. Another common pitfall: using `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` causes health check to use nodePort mapping; with passthrough you usually want `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` only if TG hits nodes.

raj: TL;DR options:
- Make sure TG target_type = ip and Service is ClusterIP/Headless exposing pod port 15020 (no nodePort required). OR
- If you must use NodePort + TG instance target_type, set externalTrafficPolicy: Local and ensure healthcheck hits nodePort on nodes that host pods.

ashley: Ok — current terraform created the TG with target_type = ip but I left the k8s Service as type=NodePort. That mismatch might be it.

devon: Yeah, that will confuse things. Also Gateway backendRef by port should be the numeric port or the exact service port name. If you reference the wrong name, the route may point at the 8080 port instead of 15020.

ashley: I'll try changing Service to ClusterIP (headless false) with the health port exposed on pod and keep TG target_type = ip. Also will rename ports to `tcp-health-15020` to avoid accidental L7 semantics.

ashley: Quick terraform snippet I changed:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "inference_health" {
  name     = "inference-health"
  port     = 15020
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    protocol = "TCP"
    port     = "15020"
  }
}
```

sre-bot: deployment-checker: canary update detected for inference (svc/inference-svc) — health failing -> 7/10 checks failed

raj: Also check iptables FORWARD rules in the node image if healthchecks keep getting rst. We've had cases where host firewall blocked pod IP:15020 for NLB checks. If your infra image locked down FORWARD, NLB -> pod IP flows can be broken.

ashley: Good call — I'll validate node firewall and flip service type. I renamed ports and updated the tf target_group health port as above. Running a quick canary.

sre-bot: healthcheck: target 10.0.12.7:15020 success

ashley: Fixed in https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/3212 — changed service to ClusterIP, renamed ports to `tcp-health-15020`, adjusted TG target_type=ip + health port 15020, validated node firewall. Canary green :thumbsup:

devon: Nice. Can you add a short note in the PR about why NodePort+ip target_type mismatch fails — saves someone else digging later.

ashley: Yep will add a comment. Thanks all!
